446: Maybe tomorrow? It's New Year, after all, and they tried too, in their own way.
447: We live outside the city—unlikely Docent can find us.
448:
All right, but don't take one step off the dacha!
Also, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife—here is her reply.
Addressed to him.
450:
- You have lunch with us on the first—promise?
- We promise!
451:
Such a pity—such a good woman, and her father is a fence,
a speculator.
452:
Why are you yelling? Who allowed you to come out?
- Here he is... A bad person.
454:
New Year has come. I wish that in this new year
everything for you is new.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
Wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you,
and I will definitely find you.
457:
- And now... one minute...
- Where'd he go?
458: Who knows? You can't make anything out with him now.
459: What is there to make out? He says he'll find us wherever—and cut our throats.
461:
They say he slit Ryaby's throat with a razor—snip, and bye-bye.
- Went completely rabid, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to you? Santa Claus has come to you,
he brought you gifts!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come on, come on. Wear them in good health—house slippers.
464:
- What the hell do I need them for? I don't even have a home.
- You will. Everything's ahead.
465:
- For now they'll come in handy in prison too. Wear them.
- All you know is to croak.
466:
This is for you, Vasya... Gavrila Petrovich, this is for you.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk like a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471: We could just sit, talk heart to heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor to talk heart to heart with you.
- We could play something.
473:
Well, I'll be... Found a sucker to play with you!
You've got nine aces in your deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game—cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
and you, with the last letter "A"—Astrakhan.
Then you, with "N"—Novgorod, you get it?
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Fine. And you, then, with "A".
- Dzhambul. - What's Dzhambul got to do with it?
480:
Because it's warm there, that's my home,
that's my mom.
481:
Then let's play like this. I'll go out, you hide something,
I come back—I find it.
482:
- You'd better find our helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We'll hide it, and he'll be peeking through a hole?
- Why? You go out and hide it.
484:
And you watch so I don't peek.
Why me? Anything happens—right away it's Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your maw open, you filthy little bastard!
- Maw, maw...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- You had a dad and mom?
- I did.
488: Why are you so mean? Why like a dog?
490:
- Came on your own.
- Ah. You're here too.
491: I was going to drop by, but I can feel it's an ambush there.
492: Mityai, I need to lay low.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Come on.
495:
- Sorry, doctor, we bothered you for nothing.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read.
499:
"Hello, dear Dad! We found out
you're in prison,
500:
and we were very happy, because we thought
you were dead."
501: Which bastard told that little Khmyr kid about Khmyr?
502:
"And Mom was happy too, because
when the letter came, she cried all day,
503:
and before that she said you were
a test pilot."
505: "And I'm happy anyway that you're alive, because Mom says
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed—swiped the shared money
and blamed it on the cabbie.
508: Beat it! I'll knock your horns off, you radish!
510:
Aren't you ashamed! You're 40 years old,
half your life is already gone.
511:
What's behind you? What's in the present?
What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it's too late. That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we need to get out of here:
That woman doctor will squeal to the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why?
- I, uh... with a razor, across her throat...
515: she's in the well, you can go look.
516: What did I have? One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten and the apartment?
Let's say ten!
520: And for a lousy 14 years I'm supposed to put up with that viper?
521:
The one the old lady put in the well?
You do what you want, I'm going to the police.
523:
And you? You'll keep putting up with him
till you die, will you?
524: Vas, I told him earlier: I've got a runny nose, and he...
525:
Enough, I'm sick of your runny nose.
Come here...
527:
- What's going on?
- We're going to beat the rug.
528:
That's it, comrades. Finita la commedia.
First of all, I'm taking this off.
530:
I'll do my time and that's it. I'll quit!
Get a job.
531:
- As what? A guard at my native collective farm.
- Why a guard?
532: I can shovel snow, lay bricks, or be a translator—I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the hat too!
What's Docent? A crook.
534:
- There's lots of crooks, but only one hat.
- If we brought in the helmet, they'd cut our time.
535: Where'd he put it? We checked everywhere.
536:
Crook! Did I tell you I've got a runny nose?
And you: Maw, maw.
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they arrested us. Remember? He says,
I'm fishing, and you dive.
539:
- Wait. What did he say about the fish then?
- I was fishing in an ice-hole,
540:
- and you, he says, Cross-Eyes, can you swim?
- He hid the helmet in the ice-hole, that's what!
541:
Exactly! I remember, bad person!
In the ice-hole—in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so? You lout! You could've left a note before hanging yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- And him?
- Forget him. Let them pick him up themselves. Carrying a hog like that. Let's go!
545:
- There's jack squat in there.
- It's there, on the bottom. You have to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens—right away it's Cross-Eyes.
Vas, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can't! It's cold, I'll get sick.
548:
- Just now he was hanging himself, now he's afraid of catching cold!
- Fitness greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd stitch you up, but I don't have time to mess around!
552:
Now it's two pieces.
And at the dacha there's another one.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich, well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
